messages:
Ivy: Heads-up — rolling gateway deploys are causing ~1-2% of in-flight streams to be orphaned when we preempt sockets. Need a lease-transfer handshake so in-flight work can be yielded safely.
Marcus: Agree. Current drain waits 30s then force-close; but upstreams sometimes continue producing after socket close and we lose terminal events, which messes SLOs.
Leila: Proposal: introduce a short-lived drain-lease header `x-rw-drain-lease: <lease-id>` that the gateway issues to the replacing instance. Lease includes TTL and owner id. The original gateway can transfer lease to the new instance via control-plane transfer RPC.
Theo: Sequence sketch: old-gw marks stream as `draining`, emits `x-rw-drain-lease: pending` to upstreams, then calls control-plane `transferLease(lease_id, new_owner)`. New-gw accepts and takes over socket ownership via ephemeral handoff. If transfer fails, old-gw finishes and emits terminal-event.
Ivy: For clients behind NAT we may not be able to hand socket to new-gw. Support two modes: in-place takeover (same socket) and logical transfer (new instance picks up stream id and resumes by reconnecting upstream). Logical transfer needs `stream-resume` semantics in upstream.
Marcus: For logical transfer, upstreams must accept resume tokens and rehydrate state. Header: `x-rw-resume-token: <opaque>` and `x-rw-resume-offset: <token-offset>`. If upstream doesn't support resume, fallback to graceful failover: emit final chunk `{"stream_status":"drain_preempted"}` so clients see deterministic termination.
Leila: Risk: resuming requires upstream idempotency for partial outputs. Add `resume_ok` capability flag in service registry; gateway only attempts transfer if upstream advertises support.
Theo: Metrics: `lease_transfers`, `lease_transfer_failures`, `resume_recoveries`, `orphaned_streams`. Also record `transfer_latency_ms` histogram.
infra-bot: FYI: adding `x-rw-drain-lease` and `x-rw-resume-token` requires WAF allowlist update and auth for control-plane RPC. Staging window Tue 04:00 UTC.
Ivy: Edge cases: hedged requests with concurrent upstreams — ensure lease goes to winning attempt. Transfer payload should include `attempt` and `winner_hint` to avoid split ownership.
Marcus: Implementation plan: 1) control-plane RPC `transferLease` + auth 2) in-memory lease store with soft-lock semantics and TTL renewals 3) resume-token generation + registry capability flag 4) final-chunk fallback for http/1.1 + trailers for h2/h3 5) dashboards/alerts + canary. Rollout under feature flag `drain-lease-transfer`.
Leila: Backcompat: if new-gw can't accept lease, old-gw falls back to existing force-close. Ensure billing labels these as `preempted` not `client_cancel` to avoid analytics skew.
Ivy: I'll draft RFC with sequence diagrams, example control-plane proto, and sample headers. Ping when draft is ready. :thumbsup:
